claims.explanation: Famciclovir is a guanine nucleoside prodrug whose active metabolite penciclovir triphosphate inhibits viral DNA polymerase; in cancer cells, selectivity likely reflects dependence on a cellular DNA polymerase or nucleotide-kinase pathway rather than a specific oncogenic driver. The pattern of sensitive lines is enriched for TP53-mutant, ARID1A-mutant, and PTEN-mutant tumors, suggesting that loss of these tumor suppressors creates replication stress or nucleotide-analog sensitivity, while KRAS-mutant lines are relatively protected. The virtual-cell response in HCC515 (a TP53-mutant lung line) supports a stress/DNA-damage response rather than a single kinase target.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set and are depleted among resistant lines
ARID1A mutations appear in many sensitive lines and are absent from most resistant lines
PTEN loss is enriched in sensitive glioma/endometrial lines
KRAS-mutant lines are overrepresented among the least affected lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma, thyroid, and glioma lines are among the most killed
RB1 loss appears in several sensitive lines (SF539, ESS1)
PIK3CA-mutant breast and endometrial lines are sensitive
NF1-mutant melanoma and sarcoma lines are sensitive
EGFR-mutant HCC4006 is among the most killed lines
CDKN2A loss appears in several sensitive lines
SMARCA4-mutant COV434 is among the least affected lines
STK11-mutant NCIH1573 is among the least affected lines
